evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/services/syndication.rs:289-406 (SyndicationService::process_syndication_job) is the ONLY code that actually acts on a queued syndication job (updates syndication status, would call the portal). A repo-wide grep for callers of `process_syndication_job` returns ZERO hits outside its own definition (`grep -rn process_syndication_job backend --include=*.rs`). Meanwhile SyndicationService::create_publish_jobs IS wired into production: routes/listings.rs:655-661 constructs a SyndicationService and calls create_publish_jobs(&listing, &data.portals, Some(tenant.user_id)) when a manager publishes a listing to portals. Net effect: publishing a listing enqueues background jobs on SYNDICATION_QUEUE that NOTHING ever drains -- there is no registered worker consuming that queue. Listings are never actually propagated to Sreality/Bezrealitky/Nehnutelnosti/etc., and the per-portal syndication status stays pending forever, with no error surfaced to the manager who requested syndication.

Even if a worker were wired up, process_syndication_job is a documented mock (syndication.rs:286-288 comment: 'This is a placeholder for the actual portal API integration. In production, this would call the respective portal APIs.'). For the PUBLISH operation it fabricates a fake external id -- `let external_id = format!("{}_{}", payload.portal, uuid::Uuid::new_v4());` (syndication.rs:318) -- and then calls listing_repo.update_syndication_status(..., syndication_status::SYNCED, Some(&external_id), None) at L321-330, i.e. it records the listing as SYNCED to the portal with a made-up external reference without any outbound portal API call. The STATUS_CHANGE / UPDATE / REMOVE arms likewise stamp SYNCED/REMOVED without contacting any portal. This is a false-success stub on a user-facing feature path (manager-initiated listing syndication, UC-31/UC-32).

Consequence: the 'publish listing to external portals' feature is silently non-functional in two compounding ways -- (1) enqueued jobs are never consumed (no drainer registered for SYNDICATION_QUEUE, unlike the push-fanout / quiet-hours-drain workers which are explicitly spawned), and (2) the processor, if ever invoked, reports success with a synthetic external id instead of integrating. Managers believe their listings reached the portals when nothing was sent. Fix: register a background worker that drains SYNDICATION_QUEUE and calls process_syndication_job, and replace the mock PUBLISH/UPDATE/REMOVE arms with real portal API calls (or gate the feature off / mark jobs failed with an explicit 'portal integration not configured' status so the UI stops claiming success). Backend fix is not cloud-landable until the api-server build block (#2966) is lifted.
